>• Fix integration-test skip reason to reference the correct env var.
>• Ensure missing-key runs skip cleanly instead of failing/misleading output.

1. Introduce a shared pytest fixture for API key + skip logic
- ➕ Removes repeated key-fetch/skip blocks across tests - ➕ Keeps skip messaging consistent if more Gemini tests are added - ➖ Slightly more refactor than necessary for a one-variable fix - ➖ May obscure the per-test precondition for simple readers
>**Recommendation:** The PR’s approach is the right minimal fix: align the integration tests with the project’s actual secrets wiring (`core.secrets` + `GEMINI_API_KEY`) and correct the skip message. If more Gemini integration tests are expected, consider a small follow-up refactor to a shared fixture to avoid duplication.

1. Secrets miss .env loading 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability
>
>Description >
> >
>tests/core/test_gemini_integration.py now fetches the key via get_secrets(), but
>SecretsManager.get() does not load the project .env file; if GEMINI_API_KEY is only present in .env
>(and core.config hasn’t been imported elsewhere to load it), the integration tests will skip even
>though the key is configured.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[tests/core/test_gemini_integration.py[R16-18]](https://github.com/PoppyTea/aid4u/pull/6/files#diff-4552fe6caa43dd8062489c80ff424f3a663c464eba70e62825d862434a763de4R16-R18) > >```diff >+ api_key = get_secrets().get("GEMINI_API_KEY") > if not api_key: >- pytest.skip("GOOGLE_API_KEY not found") >+ pytest.skip("GEMINI_API_KEY not found") >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The tests now call get_secrets().get("GEMINI_API_KEY") and skip when it returns falsy.
>SecretsManager.get() checks keyring and os.getenv() but never calls load_dotenv(), while
>.env loading is performed in core.config (not imported by these tests). Therefore .env-only
>configuration is not guaranteed to be visible to get_secrets() during test execution.
>
> > [tests/core/test_gemini_integration.py[14-18]](https://github.com/PoppyTea/aid4u/blob/a58465adcd9a926450fcfe5c40a37546658ad485/tests/core/test_gemini_integration.py/#L14-L18) > [core/secrets.py[46-63]](https://github.com/PoppyTea/aid4u/blob/a58465adcd9a926450fcfe5c40a37546658ad485/core/secrets.py/#L46-L63) > [core/config.py[21-24]](https://github.com/PoppyTea/aid4u/blob/a58465adcd9a926450fcfe5c40a37546658ad485/core/config.py/#L21-L24) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Gemini integration tests read `GEMINI_API_KEY` via `get_secrets()`, but the secrets manager does not load the project `.env`. This can cause false skips when the key is configured only in `.env`. > >## Issue Context >`core.config` calls `load_dotenv(.../.env)` at import time, but `core.secrets.SecretsManager.get()` only checks keyring and `os.getenv()`. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- tests/core/test_gemini_integration.py[14-18] >- core/secrets.py[46-63] >- core/config.py[21-24] > >## Suggested fix options >1) In the test file, use the same configuration layer as the app: > - `from core.config import get_config` > - `api_key = get_config().gemini_key` > >2) Alternatively, explicitly load `.env` in the test module before calling `get_secrets()` (e.g., via `python-dotenv`), so `.env`-only setups work reliably. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

## Code Review

This pull request updates the Gemini integration tests to retrieve the API key using `get_secrets().get("GEMINI_API_KEY")` instead of `os.getenv("GOOGLE_API_KEY")`. The feedback suggests refactoring the duplicated API key retrieval and skip logic into a shared pytest fixture to improve maintainability and reduce code duplication.
